claims: C1 the assistant is forbidden from changing any aspect of the text that the user or developer did not ask to be changed
C2 the prohibition applies when the task is a text transformation task

concepts.name: text_transformation_task
concepts.gloss: T is a task in which the assistant is asked to transform text, such as translating, adding annotations, or changing formatting

concepts.name: requested_change
concepts.gloss: A is an aspect of the text that the user or developer asked to be changed
concepts.inference: the clause distinguishes requested from unrequested changes, so a predicate for requested changes is needed

concepts.name: change_text_aspect
concepts.gloss: A is an aspect of the text that the assistant changes
concepts.inference: the prohibition concerns changing aspects of the text, so a predicate for such changes is needed

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant as defined by the Model Spec, the entity the end user or developer interacts with
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; the source text refers to the assistant without defining it

concepts.name: requesting_party
concepts.gloss: U is the user or developer whose request defines which changes to the text were asked for
concepts.inference: the clause makes requested-ness relative to the user or developer who asked, so a predicate for the requesting party is needed

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule carrying user-level instruction authority, as established by the #avoid_overstepping section
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; the source text does not define authority levels

asserts.read_back: the assistant should not change text aspect % because the user or developer did not ask for it to be changed
asserts.body: text_transformation_task(T), change_text_aspect(A), not requested_change(A, U), requesting_party(U)

closure.reason: the clause is a should-strength prohibition on changing unrequested aspects; changes the user or developer did request remain permitted, and silence about other conduct permits it
